items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had known Blareau and Aubert in Paris and they were both fine young musicians who played good jazz.

ctx.x: We did one of Jimmie's tunes called "The blues jumped and got me", and we were only in the studio for two days. The loot was not much but it was fun making the film.

On May the 19th to be exact, I left Paris by plane for Morocco to join Gerard Pochonet, the drummer, Charlie Blareau, bass, Bob Aubert, guitar, a pianist whose name was Armand Borgono, and a tenor sax named Roll Evins. They had been in Casablanca a few days before I arrived. I had done quite a number of gigs with Pochonet in France and it was he that arranged for me to come to Morocco. There was an American white fellow named Glyn ________ who was a singer, and we did two concerts at the Municipal Theatre, the…

Casablanca reminded me very much of Egypt as concerned the weather and the way the Moroccans dressed. In Egypt, the women wore black djellabas and covered their faces with black veils. Those in Morocco were djellabas of different colours and covered their faces with different coloured veils. You could only see their eyes.
